picks.t: Violent Femmes + Tune-Yards at Stern Grove
picks.d: The 89th season of Stern Grove's free concert series. 'Blister in the Sun' in the eucalyptus amphitheater is a core SF memory. Free tickets via lottery at sterngrove.org.
Free all-day festival at Jerry Garcia Amphitheater in McLaren Park. Melvin Seals & JGB, Stu Allen, The Jazz Mafia. After-parties in Excelsior bars. A love letter to SF.
Since 1974, Japantown's Peace Plaza becomes the best block party of the summer. AAPI food vendors, artisan stalls, live music on two stages. Free and genuinely one of SF's great institutions.
The violinist, songwriter, and world-class whistler joins the full orchestra at Davies Hall. His looping, genre-jumping style was built for an orchestral setting. Don't sleep on this.

picks.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs at de Young
picks.d: Artifacts from the Valley of the Kings make their U.S. debut. It'll be packed all fall — going opening weekend is the smart call. Pair with a Golden Gate Park walk.
Two nights of Grateful Dead music at the legendary outdoor amphitheater. Full show recreations down to the set lists. Go Friday, recover at Jerry Day Saturday.
Alt-country Texan rockers at the Fillmore. Hook-laden and energetic — everyone ends up knowing more words than they thought. Doors at 7.
Circus-theater love letter to SF's weird history. Aerial acrobatics, shadow play, live music. Use code 49FOR49 for $49 tickets.
Free outdoor dance showcase on the Great Lawn. Poetry workshop with Nia Pearl at noon. RSVP ahead.
Over 250 indie artists and makers at Fort Mason. Free to browse. Great for gifts and getting inspired to quit your job and make candles.
Two legends in one night at Chase Center. 'All Night Long' meets 'September.' Your parents would love this. You would too.
The beloved Filipino chain is officially open near Powell BART. Fried chicken, Jolly Spaghetti, Peach Mango Pie. Lines still long but moving.

picks.t: Living History Day at Fort Point
picks.d: Free Civil War reenactments under the Golden Gate Bridge. Meet General Grant, watch cannon demos. Surprisingly cool even if history isn't your thing.
Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rüfüs Du Sol in Golden Gate Park. 3-day sold out. Single-day still available from $249.

ongoing.d: Free concerts through Aug 16. Patti LaBelle (Aug 9), Public Enemy (Aug 15), Al Green (Aug 16). Reservations at sterngrove.org.
130+ free lunchtime concerts near Market St through late September.
Monthly evening market with food vendors, DJs, and pop-ups along the waterfront.
Free community yoga Saturdays at 10am. Bring your own mat. All levels.
Free classic arcade games, cheap drinks, DJ nights on weekends. Divisadero.
Free readings, book launches, and poetry nights in North Beach almost every week.
Every Sunday 7am–3pm. SF's oldest flea market. Free to browse, cash only.

new.name: Bar Coto
new.d: From the A16 team. Espresso, pastries, sandwiches, low-ABV cocktails. Immediately feels like it's been here for years.

new.name: Jollibee
new.d: First SF location since 2011. Fried chicken, Jolly Spaghetti, Peach Mango Pie. Lines are long but moving.

new.name: Esme
new.d: New French restaurant in the old Ragazza space. Pastas, roast chicken, cheese plates, lush back patio.

new.name: JouJou
new.d: From the Lazy Bear team. French-leaning, seafood-heavy. One of the most anticipated openings of the year.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: The taco that launched a thousand arguments. No rice, good beans, great carnitas. Cash only.

classic.name: Zuni Café
classic.d: Caesar salad, roast chicken for two, the marble bar. SF's forever restaurant.

classic.name: Absinthe
classic.d: Classic brasserie five minutes from Davies Hall. Great pre-symphony cocktails.

classic.name: Nopalito
classic.d: Thoughtful Mexican food with organic produce. Carnitas and horchata at the bar.

bars.name: Big Finish Wine
bars.d: 48 wines on tap, most under $14. Organized by finish. Nobody bothers you here.

bars.name: Bar Shoji
bars.d: Coffee by day, cocktail den at night. Wagyu-fat-washed whisky. Seamless sunset transformation.

bars.name: The DeLuxe
bars.d: Legendary jazz bar back with upgraded sound. Live music nightly, $5–15 cover.

bars.name: Valley Club
bars.d: Hotel G mezzanine. Low lights, velvet, cocoa-butter Negroni. You'll stay longer than planned.

bars.name: The Green Heron
bars.d: Took over Hobson's Choice. Classic cocktails, Miller Lite, no judgment.

bars.name: Jilli
bars.d: Makgeolli from teapots, popcorn fried chicken, kimchi vodka rigatoni. Communal and loud.

bars.name: Standard Deviant
bars.d: Waterfront taproom at Pier 70. Barrel-aged rosé-saison. Huge industrial space.

bars.name: Rikki's
bars.d: Women-focused bar. Valkyries watch parties, lavender cocktails, beer-battered wings.

sports.note: No home games this week. Next homestand starts Aug 7 vs. Cardinals. Watch at Rikki's or any sports bar.
Indie baseball with theme nights. oaklandballers.com for schedule.
Outside Lands takes over Golden Gate Park Aug 7–9. Not sports, but it'll take over the city.

concerts.d: Free at Stern Grove. 89th season. Reservations at sterngrove.org. Bring a blanket and layers.
Violin, whistling, and indie-folk with a full orchestra at Davies Hall. Genuinely special.
Night one of two Grateful Dead nights at the Greek Theatre.
Night two at the Greek. Melvin played keys with Jerry for 20 years. The real thing.
Free all-day festival at Jerry Garcia Amphitheater. After-parties in Excelsior bars.
Alt-country Texan rockers at the Fillmore. Doors at 7.
Two legends at Chase Center. 'All Night Long' meets 'September.'
Circus-theater love letter to SF. Code 49FOR49 for $49 tickets.
Broadway musical running all summer. Intimate theater, every seat is good.

concertsOngoing.d: Patti LaBelle (Aug 9), Public Enemy (Aug 15), Al Green (Aug 16). All free.
Haight St jazz bar. Jazz, soul, funk nightly. $5–15 cover.
Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rüfüs Du Sol. Single-day from $249.

singles.d: One of the best solo activities this weekend. Wander, eat, talk to artists. Free, no plan needed.
Free festival in McLaren Park. Communal energy makes talking to strangers the whole point.
Classic speed dating at a brewery. 5-minute rounds, real faces. Events sell out.
Weekly bar takeovers, rooftop parties, themed nights. Big crowds.
Kickball, soccer, volleyball, pickleball — join solo, get placed on a team.

singlesOngoing.d: November Project (free, Wed+Fri 6:30am). Midnight Runners (Thu nights). Show up, run, make friends.
Salsa and bachata lessons + open dancing. No partner needed.
Green Apple Books and City Lights host regular reading groups.
One Brick (drop-in), SF Parks Alliance, Glide Memorial.
Pottery at Claymakers, cooking at 18 Reasons, dance at ODC. Sign up solo.

date.title: Bridge, Fort & Japantown
date.tagline: Golden hour at the bridge, history at the fort, ramen in Japantown.

steps.title: Fort Point under the Golden Gate
steps.detail: Free Civil War reenactments and incredible views under the bridge. Even if history isn't your thing, the setting is unbeatable.

steps.title: Walk the bridge at sunset
steps.detail: Head up to the Golden Gate Bridge. The views at golden hour are unreal.

steps.title: Ramen in Japantown
steps.detail: Walk to Japantown after the Nihonmachi Street Fair energy. Marufuku for ramen or Sozai for izakaya.

date.title: Mission Cocktail Crawl
date.tagline: New bars, good food, and a neighborhood that rewards wandering.

steps.title: Start at Big Finish Wine
steps.detail: 48 wines on tap, most under $14. Sit at the bar, share a few glasses, ease into the evening.

steps.title: Dinner at Jilli
steps.detail: Korean communal drinking food. Makgeolli from teapots, popcorn fried chicken. Loud and fun.

steps.title: Nightcap at Bar Shoji
steps.detail: The coffee shop has transformed into a cocktail den. Wagyu-fat-washed whisky in a moody room.

date.title: Symphony & Speakeasy
date.tagline: Andrew Bird with an orchestra, then cocktails in a hidden lounge. Saturday only.

steps.title: Early dinner in Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Absinthe for pre-symphony cocktails and light bites. Five minutes from Davies Hall.

steps.title: Andrew Bird w/ the SF Symphony
steps.detail: Violin, whistling, and indie-folk performed with a full symphony. A genuinely special evening.

steps.title: Cocktails at Valley Club
steps.detail: Hotel G mezzanine. Low lights, velvet corners, cocoa-butter Negroni. The kind of place you stay longer than planned.

solo.title: Slow Morning, Big Festival
solo.tagline: Coffee, a walk, and a free all-day festival.

steps.title: Coffee at Sightglass
steps.detail: High ceilings, long tables. Bring a book or just sit. No one's in a hurry.

steps.title: Nihonmachi Street Fair
steps.detail: Wander Japantown's 52-year-old street fair. Food, art, music. Easy to spend hours.

steps.title: Jerry Day in McLaren Park
steps.detail: Free festival with live music all afternoon. Communal energy, great people-watching.

solo.title: Art, Wine & a Counter Seat
solo.tagline: A day that feels like a vacation without leaving the city.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs at de Young
steps.detail: Ancient Egyptian artifacts just opened. Go at your own pace, linger where you want.

steps.title: Lunch in the park
steps.detail: De Young cafe or walk to Nopalito on 9th Ave for pozole.

steps.title: Wine at Big Finish
steps.detail: 48 wines on tap. Grab a seat at the bar, try a few glasses. Nobody bothers you.

steps.title: Bar Shoji at sunset
steps.detail: Coffee shop transforms into cocktail den. Wagyu-fat-washed whisky and nowhere to be.

solo.title: Long Brunch, Live Music, No Phone
solo.tagline: Put your phone on DND. Today is about you.

steps.title: Brunch at Zuni Café
steps.detail: Sit at the bar, order the Caesar and oysters. Read the paper. Take an actual hour.

steps.title: Browse Green Apple Books
steps.detail: The Clement St location is a maze of used books. Get lost for an hour.

steps.title: Violent Femmes at Stern Grove
steps.detail: Free concert in the amphitheater. Bring a blanket, close your eyes. Nobody knows you're here.

steps.title: Sunset at Lands End
steps.detail: Walk the trail to the Sutro Baths ruins. Watch the Pacific. Go home when you're ready.

birthday.title: Park Hangout → Group Dinner
birthday.tagline: No pressure, no velvet ropes. Just your favorite people.

steps.title: Nihonmachi Street Fair with the crew
steps.detail: Meet everyone at Japantown. Wander, eat, listen to music. Low-effort, high-fun birthday activity.

steps.title: Dolores Park
steps.detail: Grab Bi-Rite ice cream and a blanket spot. This is the party.

steps.title: Birthday dinner at Jilli
steps.detail: Korean communal food. Makgeolli in teapots, popcorn fried chicken. Tell them it's your birthday.

birthday.title: Dinner → Live Music → Bars
birthday.tagline: A proper birthday night that builds as it goes.

steps.title: Dinner at Esme
steps.detail: New French spot in NoPa. Shareable plates, back patio, great group energy.

steps.title: Jerry Day after-party
steps.detail: If it's Saturday — the Excelsior bars will be going off after the festival. Join the energy.

steps.title: Late night at The Green Heron
steps.detail: Miller Lites and shots for the birthday person. Good bar, jukebox. Close it out.

birthday.title: Brunch → Show → Speakeasy
birthday.tagline: Go all out. It's your birthday.

steps.title: Birthday brunch at Zuni Café
steps.detail: Roast chicken for two, Caesar salad, Aperol Spritzes. Toast properly.

steps.title: Dear San Francisco at Club Fugazi
steps.detail: Circus-theater in North Beach. Aerial acrobatics, live music. Get a block of seats together.

steps.title: Champagne at Valley Club
steps.detail: Hotel G mezzanine. Order a bottle, toast the birthday person.

steps.title: Andrew Bird w/ SF Symphony
steps.detail: End the night with a full orchestra at Davies Hall. Unforgettable.

friends.title: Golden Gate to Japantown
friends.tagline: The greatest hits — done right, not touristy.

steps.title: Coffee at Equator in the Presidio
steps.detail: Good coffee in a setting that immediately says 'this city is different.'

steps.title: Walk the Golden Gate Bridge
steps.detail: Halfway and back. Yes it's windy. Your friends will take 400 photos.

steps.title: Nihonmachi Street Fair
steps.detail: Japantown's 52-year-old street fair is happening this weekend. Best AAPI food vendors, live music, art.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs at de Young
steps.detail: Egyptian artifacts just opened. Walk through Golden Gate Park to get there.

steps.title: Sunset drinks at Park Chalet
steps.detail: West end of the park, overlooking Ocean Beach. Beer garden with heat lamps.

friends.title: Mission → Dolores → Nightlife
friends.tagline: The neighborhood your friends will wish they lived in.

steps.title: Dolores Park
steps.detail: Bi-Rite ice cream, blanket spot with skyline view. Peak SF energy on a sunny day.

steps.title: Walk Valencia Street
steps.detail: Browse Paxton Gate, grab coffee at Sightglass, poke into bookstores.

steps.title: Dinner at Jilli
steps.detail: Korean communal food. Makgeolli, popcorn fried chicken. Perfect group energy.

steps.title: Bar hop on 24th
steps.detail: Big Finish for wine, then The Green Heron for nightcaps.

friends.title: Concerts, Views & Late Nights
friends.tagline: For friends who came to have a big weekend.

steps.title: Brunch at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Walk the market stalls, grab oysters, Acme bread, Blue Bottle. Sit outside on the water.

steps.title: Violent Femmes at Stern Grove
steps.detail: Free concert in the amphitheater. Bring a blanket, share wine, enjoy the fact that this is free.

steps.title: Dinner at JouJou
steps.detail: New French-California spot from the Lazy Bear team. The buzzy opening right now.

steps.title: Late night at The DeLuxe
steps.detail: Legendary jazz bar on Haight. Live music, good drinks, real SF energy.

parents.title: Parks, Views & Easy Lunch
parents.tagline: Nothing too rushed, nothing too loud. Just a beautiful day.

steps.title: Ferry Building farmers market
steps.detail: Saturday morning market. Sample olive oils, grab pastries, walk the waterfront. Parents love this.

steps.title: Lunch on the water
steps.detail: Hog Island oysters or takeaway on the benches looking at the Bay Bridge.

steps.title: Drive to Twin Peaks
steps.detail: 360° view of the entire city. Your mom will say 'wow' at least four times.

steps.title: Coffee in Noe Valley
steps.detail: 24th Street. Bernie's or Martha & Bros. Quiet, charming, easy walking.

parents.title: Museums, Music & Nice Dinner
parents.tagline: For parents who want to do something, not just see something.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs at de Young
steps.detail: Ancient Egyptian artifacts just opened. Both impressive and easy to navigate.

steps.title: Lunch in Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Absinthe for French brasserie, or walk Hayes Street for something lighter.

steps.title: Japanese Tea Garden
steps.detail: Golden Gate Park. Peaceful, beautiful. Green tea and cookies inside.

steps.title: Andrew Bird w/ SF Symphony
steps.detail: Even if your parents don't know Andrew Bird, a full orchestra in Davies Hall is universally impressive.

parents.title: Symphony & Supper Club
parents.tagline: The 'impress your parents' evening. Saturday only.

steps.title: Drinks at Absinthe
steps.detail: Classic Hayes Valley brasserie. Great cocktails, five-minute walk to Davies Hall.

steps.title: Andrew Bird w/ SF Symphony
steps.detail: Full orchestra at Davies Hall. The venue alone will get them.

steps.title: Late supper at Zuni Café
steps.detail: Roast chicken for two, Caesar salad, a bottle of something nice. Your parents will love this.
